correctness.rationale: Every perfect matching of a two-row ladder is a monomer/dimer column tiling by the even cut-crossing argument. For a deleted interior rung, all perfect matchings use either the left or right horizontal pair, giving two genuine simplicial cones. Their shared faces are exactly the join of extendible matching complexes on columns strictly to the left and right of the three blocked columns. The ordinary CW pushout is a suspension when the intersection is geometrically nonempty, with n=3,j=2 handled as two disjoint simplices. The published intact-ladder parity classification therefore yields the asserted universal homotopy type. Exhaustive graph-edge-backtracking, full-face-set comparisons and boundary reduction passed all 44 cases n=2..9. No extrapolation from finite checks is used.

value.rationale: Removing a rung in a two-row ladder merges two squares into one hexagonal defect. The full position-sensitive single-fault classification shows that an odd-width graph with an intact contractible complex can acquire a sphere whose dimension is unbounded, but only for even-position interior defects, whereas every rung fault in an even-width ladder destroys the intact sphere. The exact two-cone intersection gives a reusable structural explanation, making this a motivated topology-of-faults result rather than a small isolated computation or a renaming of the known intact case.
